subtopic: Handling a leaked photo or online harassment
subtype: Approach: blaming the victim and hiding [Pitfall]
passage:
Bhavna: Where were you today? Ma'am asked about you.
Nikita: Not coming this week. I deleted everything.
Bhavna: Everything? Nikita, why?
Nikita: It's my fault. I should never have sent it.
Bhavna: It isn't your fault. Whoever shared it did the wrong thing.
Nikita: Everyone has seen it. I can't face anyone.
Bhavna: Please let me come over. Or tell your parents?
Nikita: No. Don't tell anyone. I'm switching off my phone.
Bhavna: I can't leave it. I'm telling my mum I'm worried and I'm coming at five.
(Nikita's phone showed offline. At five Bhavna's mum was already on the phone to Nikita's parents.)

qa.q: What is Nikita feeling in this chat?
qa.a: Shame and self-blame: Nikita says it is Nikita's own fault and cannot face anyone.

qa.q: What could Nikita do instead of hiding, and why?
qa.a: Talk to a trusted adult, since the fault lies with whoever shared the picture and help can stop it spreading.

qa.q: How does the situation look to Bhavna?
qa.a: Bhavna is worried and feels helpless because Nikita is cutting off contact, so Bhavna asks a mother for help.

grounding: A teen decides it is all the teen's fault, deletes accounts and avoids school, cutting off the people who could help.

subtopic: Handling a leaked photo or online harassment
subtype: Approach: blaming the victim and hiding [Pitfall]
passage:
In their small town near Siliguri, Bidisha stopped going to school on a Monday. She told Ma it was a stomach ache. It wasn't. On Sunday a photo from her phone, her and her cousin pulling faces in their nightclothes, had turned up in a local group with rude comments. She had sent it to one friend only.
It's my fault, she thought. I shouldn't have sent it. She deleted every account she had. For five days she lay in her room with the phone off.
Meanwhile Mahima Ma'am, her class teacher, saw the photo going round the class and wanted to act, but couldn't reach Bidisha. With no one speaking up, the forwards kept going.
On Friday Ma found her crying and sat on the bed until the whole story came out. That afternoon Ma walked her to Mahima Ma'am's house. “It's not your fault,” Ma'am said gently. “Let's stop this now, together.”

qa.q: How many days did Bidisha stay in her room with the phone off?
Why did Bidisha delete every account?
qa.a: She felt ashamed and blamed herself, thinking she should never have sent the photo, and hiding seemed safer.

qa.q: What would have helped Bidisha on Monday instead of hiding?
qa.a: Telling Ma or Mahima Ma'am straight away, since adults who knew could have stopped the forwards days earlier.

qa.q: What was the week like for Mahima Ma'am?
qa.a: Mahima Ma'am wanted to act but couldn't reach Bidisha, so she watched the forwards continue, likely frustrated and worried.

grounding: Shows a teen blaming herself, deleting her accounts and staying home, and how that isolation keeps her from the people who could stop the spread.

subtopic: Handling a leaked photo or online harassment
subtype: Approach: blaming the victim and hiding [Pitfall]
passage:
In a flat in Porto, Clara pulled the blinds down on Tuesday morning and didn't go to school. The photo had gone round on Monday night: Clara in tears at a classmate's birthday party, mascara everywhere, with mocking stickers added. She kept replaying it. I shouldn't have gone. I shouldn't have cried in front of anyone. It's on me.
She deleted her accounts one after another and switched her phone off. Her friend Yara had already told the head of year, who wanted to talk to Clara. Yara messaged, then called, then came to the door. Clara didn't answer. By Thursday, without Clara there to say what happened, the school still hadn't found who started it, and the photo reached another year group.
On Thursday evening her dad came home early, found the blinds still down, and sat on her floor. After an hour she told him. He phoned the head of year before dinner.

qa.q: When did Clara's dad come home early?
What was Clara thinking as she replayed the photo?
qa.a: Clara felt ashamed and blamed herself, thinking she shouldn't have gone or cried in front of anyone.

qa.q: Which choice could have helped Clara more than hiding?
qa.a: Answering Yara and going in to talk to the head of year, so the school could act while the photo was still in one group.

qa.q: What was it like for Yara, trying to reach Clara?
qa.a: Yara was probably worried and helpless, having already told the head of year but unable to get Clara to answer.

grounding: Shows a teen blaming herself, deleting her accounts and staying home, and how the isolation cuts her off from those trying to stop the spread.
